origins.summary: Among the installed study references, this file is closest to Admixed American study references. The closest study-group comparison is Puerto Rican in Puerto Rico. These comparisons use 11,071 aligned markers across 22 autosomes. Nearby results overlap: Puerto Rican in Puerto Rico; African Ancestry in Southwest USA; Colombian in Medellin. The names describe reference participants, not a fixed personal ethnic identity.

calibration.plain: In an internal test of 130 excluded public reference donors, the unrounded similarity method recovered 87 study labels and the correct broad group for 125 donors. This small reference-only diagnostic is not your probability of belonging to a group; consumer-array masks, relatives, mixed ancestry and out-of-reference populations need further validation. Rounded scores can tie.

modern.comparison_method: Broad scores are the best named-reference score in each region. Ties use one-decimal display precision; nearby references are within 0.5 score units as a descriptive display convention. Coverage labels require 1,000 markers on 10 autosomes and are not a calibrated ancestry probability.

ancient.headline: Ancient groups compared across 4,426 common markers
ancient.plain: The leading ancient-reference scores are tied at the displayed precision: Anatolian early farmer references; Caucasus hunter-gatherer references; Eastern hunter-gatherer references; Zagros early farmer references; Steppe early Bronze Age references; Western hunter-gatherer references. No unique closest ancient group is resolved. Every group was compared on the same 4,426 directly called markers. Of these, 0 homozygous calls occur at loci where the reference groups have different allele frequencies; those are the calls that can distinguish these groups with this score. This describes shared variation, not the fraction of your DNA inherited from that group.

groups.short_plain: Published Neolithic individuals from Barcin and Mentese in northwestern Anatolia.
groups.limitations: Descriptive shared-allele affinity to a small curated reference set, not inherited DNA percentage, ethnicity, direct descent or a fitted admixture model. Ancient individuals span different eras and sites; capture ascertainment, missing calls, pseudohaploid sampling, residual error, linkage and reference selection affect scores. Small groups are particularly uncertain. No consumer-ancestry calibration.

ancient.comparison_method: Every group uses the same directly called loci. Equal one-decimal scores are tied; nearby groups fall within 0.5 score units. These are display conventions, not calibrated statistical uncertainty.

score_diagnostics.score_explainer: Each heterozygous call contributes exactly 50/100 to every group. Group ordering comes only from homozygous calls at loci whose ancient group frequencies differ. A high absolute sharing score can reflect common alleles and does not establish a specific origin; 50 is not an average-human baseline.
score_diagnostics.contrast_explainer: Relative-to-panel-mean values subtract the equally weighted mean of the 6 compared group scores at the same loci. They express score differences in points, not ancestry fractions or statistical significance.
score_diagnostics.shared_alleles_explainer: Compared allele copies are two per direct diploid call. Shared-allele equivalents are an expectation using ancient group frequencies and may be fractional; they are not a count of exact ancient-person matches.

rank_stability.method: Recompute the same shared-allele score after removing each covered chromosome once. Each run retains at least 50 loci on two chromosomes. Counts and score ranges are a sensitivity check, not a confidence interval, ancestry probability, or independent validation.

equal_chromosome_weighting.method: Average the per-chromosome scores with equal chromosome weights to reveal sensitivity to marker density. This is a diagnostic alternative, not a replacement ancestry estimate.

rank_stability.plain: The pooled scores do not resolve a unique leading group; chromosome-omission results are shown without assigning confidence to an arbitrary winner.
